description: Renovate runs from .github/workflows/renovate.yaml rather than the hosted app: installing the app needs rights on the account that were not available.

It replaces Dependabot rather than joining it. Dependabot handles gomod, github-actions and npm natively but cannot see the three tool versions pinned inside ci.yaml's env, which is the entire reason this exists — and two bots on the same ecosystems means two pull requests for one bump.

The schedule is the WHOLE of Monday, so weekly batches land in one review. The workflow's cron decides how often Renovate runs; this decides what it may do when it runs. A manual workflow_dispatch sets RENOVATE_FORCE and ignores it, which is how the first pass happens without waiting.
rebaseWhen keeps branches current because protection on main is strict: without it a pull request goes stale as soon as anything else lands.

customManagers.description: The three tool versions in ci.yaml's env, which no built-in manager reads. The `renovate:` comment above each pin carries the datasource and depName, so this pattern knows no special cases — the three are not homogeneous: Go modules for govulncheck and actionlint, PyPI for zizmor. A test in internal/ci reads this regex out of this file and asserts it still matches every annotated pin AND that every pin is annotated, because the failure mode is silent: Renovate opens no pull request, for ever, and nothing says so.

packageRules.description: A pinned tool or action changes what CI does, not what this module gives a consumer, so it releases nothing: ci is not a releasable type. See docs/releases.md.

The module graph is test-only today — testify and its transitives. chore releases nothing, which is right for that. A dependency that reaches the commands themselves would need a type semantic-release acts on, so adding one is a change here as well.
semantic-release and its preset. They shape releases and ship nothing to a consumer.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Exempt from the Monday schedule: a fix should not wait for a batch.
